families.name: gemm:K4096
families.notes: GemmCoordinate K=4096 (q/k/v projections, router logits, expert gate+up for the 8 routed experts)

families.name: gemm:K8192
families.notes: GemmCoordinate K=8192 (o_proj over NH*HD)

families.name: gemm:K1536
families.notes: GemmCoordinate K=1536 (expert down projection, 8 routed experts)

families.name: gemm:K4096:lm_head
families.notes: GemmCoordinate K=4096 (lm_head, V rows)

families.name: attn:qk:f32
families.notes: s_k = q.k_k (128-long bf16 dot, f32), 64 per block

families.name: attn:p:bf16
families.notes: p_k = bf16(exp2((s_k - m_ref)*scale)); (a): m_ref = running max; (a'): m_ref = the block's max

families.name: attn:blockmax:f32
families.notes: (a') m_b = max(s_1..s_64) of the block (block-local, not running)

families.name: attn:rownorm:f32
families.notes: (a') l = sum_b exp2((m_b - m*)*scale) * sum_k p_bk, m* = max_b m_b; replays the block rescale internally

families.name: attn:outcoord:bf16
families.notes: (a') o_j = bf16( sum_b exp2((m_b - m*)*scale) * sum_k p_bk V_bkj / l ): one VU per (row, coordinate), the block-wise rescaled accumulation replayed internally; 128 per (query, head)

families.name: rms:sumsq:f32
families.notes: ss = sum_i x_i^2 over H (2 per layer + 1 final norm at output positions)

families.name: rms:rsqrt:f32
families.notes: r = rsqrt(ss/H + eps)

families.name: rms:scale:bf16
families.notes: y_i = bf16(x_i * r * w_i), H per row

families.name: qknorm:sumsq:f32
families.notes: q/k head norm: ss over HD, per (layer, q head or kv head)

families.name: qknorm:rsqrt:f32
families.notes: q/k head norm: rsqrt

families.name: qknorm:scale:bf16
families.notes: q/k head norm: HD per head

families.name: rope:out:bf16
families.notes: o_j = bf16(x_j cos_j -/+ x_j' sin_j), HD per (layer, head)

families.name: elem:residual:bf16
families.notes: bf16(x_i + o_i), 2 per layer x H

families.name: elem:silu_mul:bf16
families.notes: bf16(silu(a_i) * b_i), 8 routed experts x DE

families.name: moe:combine:bf16
families.notes: bf16(sum_{j<8} w_j y_ji), H per layer

families.name: embed:gather:bf16
families.notes: e_i = Emb[id][i], H per position

families.name: router:max:f32
families.notes: max over E f32 logits

families.name: router:exp:f32
families.notes: e_i = exp(l_i - max), E per layer

families.name: router:sum:f32
families.notes: sum_i e_i

families.name: router:prob:f32
families.notes: p_i = e_i / sum, E per layer

families.name: router:topk_id
families.notes: id_j = argmax of the probs minus the j earlier ids: 7-bit expert index, 8 per layer

families.name: router:topk_w:f32
families.notes: w_j = p_{id_j} / sum_j' p_{id_j'}, 8 per layer

families.name: tokenselect:id18
families.notes: argmax over V logits -> one token id (18-bit index unit)

families.name: Input[weights]
families.exception: prescribed; not a VU; not sampled; enforced by statement validation
families.notes: prescribed input: the bf16 parameters of the registered program (one entry per parameter, referenced from the registered commitment, never recommitted); count equals the HF safetensors parameter count; not a VU, not sampled

families.name: Input[prompt]
families.exception: prescribed; not a VU; not sampled; enforced by statement validation
families.notes: prescribed input: prompt token ids, 18-bit index (ceil(log2 V)); the serving container is 32-bit; not a VU, not sampled

N_V.note: A1: inputs are prescribed values, not VUs, not sampled; they are not in N_V and add no term to the Bound

A_tight.formula: max_cut + ceil(log2(e*N/k)); N = M*N_V; k = s*q*N
A_tight.note: relation VUs across M requests, each acquired with its RU at probability q and then sampled at s; prescribed inputs add no term; e*N/k = e/(s*q) so the table does not depend on N

interior_bytes_per_RU.includes: outgoing interface words of every request-local relation VU at actual widths (S.out of the unit)
interior_bytes_per_RU.excludes: weight inputs (prescribed; referenced from the registered commitment, never recommitted); the request's prompt-token and seed inputs and its served output tokens (committed at serve time)
interior_bytes_per_RU.note: served output tokens are produced by request-local VUs and so are inside `bits`; they are < 1e-6 of it and are not subtracted
interior_bytes_per_RU.verified_by_L5_A1: words/bits re-summed from the relation families only (every Input[...] family excluded): equal to the emitted values; weights and request inputs were never inside this volume

provenance.label: MODELED
provenance.method: per-position multiplicities x positions; attention per (layer, head, query row) over ceil(T/64) 64-key blocks at cache length T (query at position T attends T keys) under the dual-chunk-attention carrier SCALAR-VU assumed (chunk 131072, local 4096; <= 2 boundary partials per pass counted as full blocks, one 3-way merge per row once T > 131072)
provenance.block_size_basis: assumed 64-key blocks per the batch-invariant attention kernel (DIRECTIVE §1.5.4; label: assumed)
provenance.kappa: the scalar's own storage width (every relation emits exactly one scalar; bf16 16 / f32 32 / expert id 7 / token id 18)
provenance.widths: asserted in code: out_scalars == 1 for every family; widths from the relation definition (no program exists to read a boundary from)
provenance.ru: one RU per request (the whole request's computation): the partition analogue of SMALL's P1/cu=whole (orchestrator ruling vi)
provenance.moe_routing: expert GEMM / silu / combine coordinates counted for the routed top-8 experts per token under balanced routing (DEFAULT TAKEN, MODELED)
provenance.notes_inputs: Input[weights] and Input[prompt] are prescribed inputs (A1); SMALL tonight keeps them as P1's per-request input units (per-RU-copy formulation, sampled: true, digest unchanged). The program has no seed input gate (greedy decoding: token selection is deterministic).
